Organic materials often break down more easily.
Some are kinder to the environment.
What is an inorganic material?
A material that usually comes from living things
A material that comes from nonliving sources such as rocks, metals, and minerals
A synthetic polymer with no mineral core
Processed wood that still contains plant cells
Inorganic materials come from nonliving sources—rocks, metals, glass, and clay are examples.
They can be natural or made by people.
They often do not break down as easily as organic materials.

Dry wood that is not attracted to a magnet
A material that is attracted to a magnet (for example, iron)
Aluminum that is usually not attracted to a household magnet
Thick glass that is not attracted to a magnet
Magnetic materials are pulled toward a magnet. Iron, nickel, and cobalt are examples. Not all metals are magnetic.
Magnets attract magnetic materials.

A material that stretches and then returns to its original shape
A material that stays sticky forever after you press it
A material that cracks in the cold and never changes again
An elastic material can stretch or bend and then go back to its original shape—like rubber or a spring.
Elasticity is a useful material property.
Many products work because of elastic materials.

Both are defined only by weight, not by how many times you can use them
Reusable materials can be used again; disposable ones are meant for one use
Disposable materials are always stronger and better for long use than reusable ones
Reusable materials must always be artificial and become dangerous faster
Reusable items can be used again and again, like a glass bottle. Disposable items are meant for one use, like a single-use plastic bag.
Using reusable materials helps protect the environment.
It reduces waste.
What is in the universe?
Earth as the only body in the universe
Stars, planets, moons, and many galaxies
Only the solar system with no other galaxies
Only moons that orbit Earth
The universe holds stars, planets (like Earth), moons, and many galaxies. It is enormous.
The universe is vast beyond everyday imagination.
Earth is only a tiny part of it.
How many moons does Earth have?
Zero
One
Two
Three
Earth has one moon. It orbits Earth and is often simply called the Moon.
The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
We see it because it reflects sunlight.
What is the Sun?
A star that gives Earth light and heat.
A planet that orbits around Earth.
A moon that travels around Earth.
A very large planet made mostly of ice.
The Sun is a star — the closest star to Earth. It provides the light and heat that make life on Earth possible. All planets in our solar system orbit the Sun.
The Sun is a star at the center of our solar system.
All the planets, including Earth, orbit the Sun.
What are the four seasons?
There is only one season — hot weather throughout the whole year.
Spring, summer, fall, and winter — each with different weather patterns.
Only cold and rainy seasons exist in all places on Earth.
The weather never really changes, so there are no real seasons.
Earth has four seasons — spring, summer, fall, and winter — caused by Earth's tilt as it orbits the Sun. Different parts of Earth receive more or less sunlight at different times of year.
Earth's axial tilt causes different parts to receive more or less sunlight throughout the year.
Seasons are the result of Earth's orbit combined with its tilt.
What is a planet?
A body that produces its own light and heat like the Sun.
A large body that orbits a star, such as Earth orbiting the Sun.
An object that orbits another planet.
Any small object that travels through space between planets.

A planet is a large, roughly spherical body that orbits a star. In our solar system, eight planets orbit the Sun. Planets do not produce their own light — we can see them because they reflect sunlight. Earth, Mars, and Jupiter are all planets.
Our solar system has eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
Planets are kept in their orbits by the gravitational pull of the Sun.
Which statement best describes a planet?
A planet is any small object that orbits other planets.
A large body in space that orbits a star and does not produce its own light.
A planet is a type of moon that orbits the Sun directly.
A small glowing object that travels quickly across the night sky.
A planet is a large body that orbits a star. Unlike stars, planets do not make their own light.
Earth is a planet that orbits the Sun.
Moons orbit planets, not stars directly.
What is an asteroid?
A massive body that makes its own light
A large rock in space that orbits the Sun
A heavy body that orbits a star like Earth does as a planet
A satellite that orbits only Earth
An asteroid is a rocky body in space that orbits the Sun. Many are found between the planets.
Asteroids are leftovers from the early solar system.
Some are tiny; some are large.
How is a planet different from a star?
A planet has its own inner fire that makes it glow in the night sky.
A planet orbits a star and does not produce its own light.
A planet is always much bigger than any star.
A planet is exactly the same as Earth in size and shape.
A planet orbits a star and does not produce its own light — it reflects sunlight. A star, like our Sun, produces its own light and heat.
Planets travel in nearly circular orbits around a star.
Our Sun is the star at the center of our solar system.
What is a galaxy?
A single star in the solar system
A huge group of stars, planets, and gases
A moon that orbits Earth
A single comet with only a short tail
A galaxy is a huge collection of millions or billions of stars, planets, gas, and dust held by gravity.
There are many galaxies in the universe.
Our galaxy is called the Milky Way.
What is a black hole?
A dark empty place in space
A region in space with gravity so strong that even light cannot escape
A dead star with no gravity at all
A massive moon that blocks light because of its shadow
A black hole has gravity so strong that even light cannot escape. One can form when a very massive star collapses.
Black holes are still mysterious to scientists.
Researchers continue to study them.
What should you do with trash?
Leave it beside the bin if the recycling station bin is full
Put it in a trash bin or the right recycling container
Pack everything into one bag with no sorting to save space
Collect only paper at home and dump the rest into the same street bin
Trash belongs in a bin or the correct recycling container to keep the environment clean and healthy.
Bins are meant for collecting waste.
How can you help protect nature?
Feed wild animals cooked food so visitors can get closer
Do not litter outdoors, and keep natural places clean
Pick rare wild plants to take home as souvenirs
Build trails without protecting sensitive habitats
You help nature by not littering, keeping places clean, and respecting plants and animals.
Nature matters for people and for all living things.
Everyone can help protect it.
What is air pollution?
Completely clean air with no pollutants
Harmful materials in the air that damage health and the environment
Sunlight that blocks gases from entering the system
Air pollution is harmful material in the air from cars, factories, and other sources that can hurt health and nature.
It often comes from human activity.
It can lead to illness.
What is water pollution?
Channel water that is always pure
Adding harmful materials to water that cause damage
A fully clear lake with no microbes
A sweet stream that never carries sediment
Water pollution means harmful materials such as waste or chemicals enter water and harm living things that need clean water.
It can hurt nature and people.
Keeping water clean is important.
What is soil pollution?
When soil is mixed with fertilizer to help plants grow better.
When harmful materials like chemicals or trash get into the soil and damage living things.
When plants stop growing because the soil is too dry.
When soil is moved from one place to another by wind or water.
Soil pollution happens when harmful substances enter the soil and damage the plants, animals, and people who depend on it.
Pollution in the soil affects everything that grows in it.
Chemicals from factories and improperly disposed trash are common sources of soil pollution.
What is the greenhouse effect?
When the glass in a real greenhouse breaks and lets cold air inside.
When gases in Earth's atmosphere trap heat from the Sun and warm the planet.
When the Earth is always very cold because the Sun is too far away.
When sunlight simply makes plants grow faster in spring.
The greenhouse effect happens when certain gases in the atmosphere trap heat from the Sun, keeping Earth warm enough for life. Too much of this effect can cause the planet to overheat.
Greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and water vapor trap heat in the atmosphere.
More greenhouse gases mean more heat is trapped, which can warm the planet too much.
What is climate?
The weather conditions that change from day to day.
The long-term pattern of weather in a region over many years.
The temperature recorded on just one single day.
The amount of rainfall measured in just one week.
Climate is the long-term average of weather conditions in a region. It differs from weather, which describes conditions on a single day.
Climate describes patterns over decades, while weather describes today's conditions.
Different regions have different climates, such as tropical, desert, or polar.
What is a nature reserve?
Land set aside for continuous city building
A protected area for nature, animals, and plants
A crowded neighborhood with no parks
An industrial site with open waste centers
A nature reserve is a protected place where plants and animals are guarded. People may visit carefully without harming wildlife.
Reserves help protect species of animals and plants.
They matter for future generations.
What does sustainability mean?
Using as many natural resources as possible as fast as you can.
Using resources carefully and responsibly so they are available for future generations.
Only thinking about nature for one special day each year.
Ignoring the environment so that businesses can grow faster.
Sustainability means using resources like water, energy, and materials in ways that do not run out or damage the environment, so future generations can meet their own needs too.
Sustainable practices include recycling and using renewable energy sources.
Sustainability protects Earth's resources for future generations.

Be careful, read the instructions, and get help from an adult
Start with the strongest material without reading the steps
Skip organizing equipment if time is short
Before an experiment, stay careful and get adult help. Also think about what you want to test.
Safety is very important in experiments.
An adult should help and supervise.
What is an observation in a science experiment?
A prediction made before the experiment begins.
Information gathered using your senses — what you see, hear, smell, taste, or feel.
The final written answer at the end of the experiment.
A math equation used to calculate a result.

An observation is something you notice using your senses during an experiment. Good scientists describe exactly what they see, hear, or measure without guessing why it happened. Observations are the raw evidence that leads to conclusions.
Observations describe what is actually happening, not what you think will happen.
Careful, detailed observations make experiments more reliable and trustworthy.
